issues.summary: runQuickBenchmark() captures no SD error code when the raw sector read fails, unlike its open/write/read/verify failure paths
issues.suggestion: In runQuickBenchmark(), immediately after the rawReadAtCurrentSpeed() call, if !result.rawReadOk call recordSdError(sd, result.ioErrorCode, result.ioErrorData, "RAW READ") — mirroring exactly what spi_scale_benchmark.cpp already does at its own rawReadAtCurrentSpeed() call site. No signature change needed since the SD error state is still valid immediately after the failed call returns.
evidence: benchmark.cpp:499-504: `result.rawReadOk = rawReadAtCurrentSpeed(buffer, BENCH_TEST_SIZE, result.rawReadMBs);` passes no error out-params, while the open/write/read/verify paths just above it (lines 443-487) all thread `result.ioErrorCode`/`result.ioErrorData` through.
benchmark_raw.cpp:66-84: rawReadAtCurrentSpeed() does call recordSdError() on failure, but stores the code/data into local stack variables that go out of scope on return — the caller never sees them.

spi_scale_benchmark.cpp:94-105 shows the pattern that would close this gap: after rawReadAtCurrentSpeed() fails there, it calls recordSdError(sd, point.errorCode, point.errorData, "BENCH") a second time to capture the code into its own result struct.

add.description: hz, spi, crc, cid, csd, fs, and mid are not project-invented shorthand - they mirror SdFat's own field/register names (cid_t.mid, csd_t) and standard SD terminology, so the abbreviations are self-documenting to anyone familiar with the hardware domain and are used identically at every call site.

add.header: Getter functions verified free of side effects
add.description: getSd(), getCardInfo(), getAttempts(), and getAttemptCount() in hardware/sd_card.h/.cpp were checked and each does nothing but return a reference/pointer to already-computed static state - no getX-that-mutates naming/behavior mismatch exists in the codebase.

add.header: All three prior naming_quality findings confirmed fixed
add.description: readTouch()'s screenX/screenY rename, the showDiagnosticsScreen()/uiShowDiagnostics() collision (resolved by inlining into main.cpp's showDiagnostics()), and printCardIdentity() -> printCardReport() were each re-verified directly in the current source with no partial or regressed fixes.

add.header: All extractable pure logic now has native Unity coverage
add.description: bench_math, card_format, card_identity, touch_calibration, ui_geometry, and app_types are each covered by a dedicated native test suite compiled via platformio.ini's env:native build_src_filter, closing every previously-identified test gap in hardware-independent code.

add.header: Tests are value-based with strong edge-case coverage, no snapshots
add.description: Every suite asserts concrete expected values (known CRC vectors, hand-computed geometry, boundary clamps) and explicitly exercises edge cases like divide-by-zero guards and all-failed states, rather than relying on snapshot comparisons -- this keeps the suite resistant to false failures from incidental implementation changes.

add.header: CI enforces the native test suite on every push/PR
add.description: .github/workflows/native-tests.yml runs `pio test -e native`, so the test suite is a hard gate rather than a suite developers must remember to run manually.

add.header: Hardware-coupled orchestration logic has zero automated coverage
add.description: scanCard()'s per-speed qualification loop, runQuickBenchmark()'s prealloc/write/read/verify/cleanup sequencing, runSpiScalingBenchmark(), and main.cpp's event loop all require Arduino/SdFat/TFT_eSPI and have no native-testable path or mock harness, so this control-flow layer relies entirely on physical-hardware validation even though it is core business logic.

add.header: Acyclic core->hardware->{ui,benchmark} layering
add.description: coupling_matrix shows every cross-directory edge points from a higher layer to a lower one (ui/benchmark -> hardware -> core), with no reciprocal edges and no ui<->benchmark coupling -- this is the load-bearing structural property of the codebase and should be preserved as new features are added.

add.header: benchmark/ no longer depends upward on ui/
add.description: benchmark.cpp's #include list confirms ui/display_ui.h was removed; runQuickBenchmark() now takes a BenchmarkProgressFn callback (defined in benchmark.h) and main.cpp passes uiShowProgress in, so the domain layer stays presentation-agnostic. Any future long-running domain operation needing progress reporting should follow this same callback-injection pattern rather than including a ui header directly.

add.header: main.cpp at src root is the PlatformIO entry point, not a straggler
add.description: src/main.cpp is the only root-level file; it's the framework-mandated Arduino/PlatformIO build entry point (imports from all four subpackages to compose them), not evidence of missing organization.

add.header: ui/ splits one logical component (display_ui.h) across per-screen .cpp files
add.description: display_ui.cpp, display_diagnostics.cpp, display_progress.cpp, and display_results.cpp each implement a subset of display_ui.h's declared functions and share display_ui_internal.h for private helpers (tft(), header(), lineRow()) -- a deliberate one-header/many-.cpp split for compilation-unit size, not accidental fragmentation. benchmark/ uses the same *_internal.h convention (benchmark_internal.h), giving both multi-file directories a consistent internal-header pattern.
